title: A Tg-shifted Andrade coordinate better compresses viscosity-temperature curves
quantitative_support: 39 samples, 4559 raw points; simple median R2=0.9967; Tg-shifted median R2=0.9997; 38/39 improve; median ln-viscosity RMSE reduction=65.3%.
claim: Within the source 40-80 C range, a polyol-Tg shift materially improves the compact temperature representation for most formulations.
limitations: Two formulations remain below R2=0.98 even after Tg shift; this is model compression, not a universal constitutive law.

title: Free NCO couples viscosity level and thermal sensitivity
quantitative_support: 11/11 high-quality chemistry families show lower fitted viscosity with increasing free NCO. Median +1 wt%-point NCO multipliers: eta45=0.709, eta75=0.736; median dEa/dNCO=-0.81 kJ/mol per wt%-point.
claim: Stoichiometry changes both absolute viscosity and the temperature dependence of flow; the NCO effect is stronger at lower temperature in the measured range.
limitations: Family slopes are descriptive and based on a finite chemistry panel.

title: Lower temperature amplifies matched chemistry contrast
quantitative_support: For 7 matched C/P pairs, median C/P ratio=8.85 at 45 C vs 4.63 at 75 C; median amplification=1.91x; median delta Ea=19.89 kJ/mol.
claim: Temperature changes the magnitude of chemistry contrast rather than merely applying a universal multiplicative shift.
limitations: Ratios are evaluated from high-quality fits at temperatures inside the source measurement window.

title: Global rankings can remain stable while local temperature-induced inversions occur
quantitative_support: 37 high-quality samples: Spearman rho(45 vs 75)=0.959, Kendall tau=0.871; 43/666 pairwise inversions (6.46%). 6/12 matched D/P pairs have fitted crossovers inside their joint measured ~40-80 C range.
claim: A high global rank correlation does not guarantee formulation-order preservation across processing temperature.
limitations: Crossovers are inferred from per-sample fits, though inside the measured temperature range.

title: A direct patent example confirms temperature-induced rank inversion
quantitative_support: US5932680A Example 1 vs Example 4: 190 vs 98 Pa.s at 90 C, but 55 vs 60 Pa.s at 110 C; fitted crossover ~109.5 C.
claim: Temperature-dependent formulation ranking is not only a fitted-curve artifact; a direct inversion is present in an independent patent dataset.
limitations: Example 4 has two reported temperature points; fitted crossover is interpolative, while the rank inversion itself is directly observed.

title: Polyester composition response is context dependent
quantitative_support: US5932680A Examples 5-8: high-A/low-A eta130 ratio=1.654 in C/D-balanced background vs 1.091 in D-rich background; ratio-of-ratios=1.516; difference-of-differences=15.0 Pa.s.
claim: The rheological effect of a composition shift depends on surrounding blend context, inconsistent with a universal additive response.
limitations: No replicate variance is reported for the four patent points; effect-size statement only.

title: Rheology should be represented as a state, not a single-temperature scalar
quantitative_support: Under ln(eta)=A+Ea/(RT), a formulation is specified by a reference viscosity and thermal-sensitivity coordinate. Temperature amplification and crossovers follow from differences in Ea.
claim: Use (eta_ref, Ea_app) or an equivalent Tg-shifted state representation for temperature-aware screening and inverse design.
limitations: The simple apparent-Ea coordinate is an engineering compression; Tg-shifted Andrade is more accurate for the Pugar library.
